title: CLI fails to match files on Windows-style backslash paths
description:
On Windows, running the CLI with a backslash-style path (e.g. .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html) fails with "No matching .html or .php files found for: ..." even though the file exists.

Root cause: src/cli.js:66 passes raw argv patterns directly into fast-glob (fg). fast-glob treats backslash as a glob escape character, not a path separator, so a pattern like .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html gets mangled into .\tests\fixturesmastermind-lsparts\footer.html (backslash + following char is consumed as an escape sequence) and never matches.

Repro (confirmed):
- fg([".\\tests\\fixtures\\mastermind-ls\\parts\\footer.html"]) -> []
- fg(["./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html"]) -> matches correctly

Reported via: `npm start .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` and `npx . .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` both failing.

Suggested fix: normalize backslashes to forward slashes on each pattern before passing to fast-glob in src/cli.js, so Windows-style paths are supported.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** CLI fails to match files when given Windows-style backslash paths

**Current behavior:**
When a user passes a file pattern using Windows-style backslashes (e.g.
`.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`) as a CLI argument, the
CLI reports "No matching .html or .php files found" even though the file
exists. This happens because the glob library used to resolve patterns
treats backslash as an escape character, not a path separator, so
backslash-delimited patterns are silently mangled and never match. This
affects `.\`, `..\`, and any other pattern using `\` as a separator, on
Windows only.

**Desired behavior:**
On Windows, file patterns using backslash separators resolve correctly and
match the same files their forward-slash equivalent would, with no manual
conversion required from the user. On non-Windows platforms, backslash
handling is unchanged (it retains its glob-escape meaning there).

**Key interfaces:**
- The function that turns CLI argv into glob patterns should normalize
  path separators (`\` → `/`) per pattern before handing them to the glob
  resolver, but only when running on Windows (`process.platform ===
  'win32'`). Do not normalize on other platforms — backslash is a legal
  filename character and glob-escape character there.
- No change to the glob resolver's matching semantics or its output shape
  (array of matched file paths) is needed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] On Windows, a pattern like `.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`
      resolves to the same file(s) as `./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html`
- [ ] Existing forward-slash pattern behavior is unchanged on all platforms
- [ ] A new test passes a raw backslash-style pattern as CLI argv (not
      routed through any existing test helper that pre-normalizes
      separators) and asserts a match on Windows
- [ ] On non-Windows platforms, patterns containing `\` are passed through
      unmodified, preserving glob-escape semantics

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the existing fixture-path test helper that pre-normalizes
  separators for other tests — it serves a different purpose (portable
  fixture paths) and should stay as-is
- Any other cross-platform path handling issues not related to glob
  pattern matching

comments.text:
## Implementation summary

Fixed the Windows backslash-glob bug at the single call site that matters: `src/cli.js`.

**Change:**
- Added `normalizePatternsForPlatform(patterns, platform = process.platform)` (exported, pure) in `src/cli.js`, just above `main()`. On `win32` it maps each pattern through `p.split('\\').join('/')`; on every other platform it returns `patterns` unchanged.
- `main()` now calls `fg(normalizePatternsForPlatform(patterns), ...)` instead of `fg(patterns, ...)` — the only `fg(`/`fast-glob` call site in `src/` (confirmed by grep), so this is the single choke point, not scattered.

**Why this shape:** fast-glob treats `\` as a glob-escape character, not a path separator, so a Windows-style pattern like `.\tests\fixtures\...\footer.html` gets mangled (backslash + next char consumed as an escape) and never matches. Converting `\`→`/` only on win32 preserves `\` as a legal glob-escape/filename character on POSIX platforms, per the ticket's explicit non-goal.

## Tests added (`tests/cli.test.js`)

1. **CLI-level regression test** (`it.skipIf(process.platform !== 'win32')`): builds the argv pattern as a literal relative backslash string (`'.\\tests\\fixtures\\wp-block-guard\\unbalanced-delimiter.html'`) — deliberately *not* routed through the existing `fx()` helper (which pre-normalizes separators for portability and is out of scope to touch) — spawns the real CLI binary via `spawnSync`, and asserts the backslash run produces the same exit status and JSON report as the forward-slash equivalent. Uses `unbalanced-delimiter.html`, an existing fixture that trips a Layer-1 structural error, so block-runner (Layer 2) is skipped and the test stays fast (no long timeout needed).
   - Used `it.skipIf` rather than an early `if (process.platform !== 'win32') return`, since an early return would report as a *passing* test on non-Windows CI, masking the fact it never ran.
2. **Unit tests for `normalizePatternsForPlatform`**: backslash→forward-slash conversion on `'win32'`, forward-slash patterns left unchanged on `'win32'`, and backslash patterns passed through unmodified on `'linux'`/`'darwin'` (platform injected as a parameter, no `process.platform` mocking needed).

**Red/green verification:** before finalizing, I temporarily reverted the `fg()` call to the pre-fix form and re-ran the new CLI-level test in isolation — it failed (`AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1`, i.e. the backslash run exited 2/"no matching files" while the forward-slash run succeeded), confirming the test actually discriminates. Restored the fix immediately after.

## Full test suite

`npx vitest run` → **47/47 passing** (4 test files) on this run. Note: on two earlier runs, `tests/pipeline.test.js`'s two `--fix` tests (`fixes a near-miss block in place...`, `fixes a file with multiple BLOCK_INVALID findings...`) timed out at 45000ms due to slow/cold block-runner process spawns — this is **pre-existing flakiness unrelated to this change**. I confirmed this by `git stash`-ing my changes and re-running the same test against unmodified `develop` code; it failed identically (same 45000ms timeout). Not touched, per the ticket's stated out-of-scope.

## Files changed
- `src/cli.js` — added `normalizePatternsForPlatform()`, wired into the `fg()` call in `main()`.
- `tests/cli.test.js` — added the regression test and the `normalizePatternsForPlatform` unit tests described above.

## Acceptance criteria checklist
- [x] Windows backslash pattern resolves to the same file(s) as its forward-slash equivalent
- [x] Forward-slash pattern behavior unchanged on all platforms (existing suite unaffected + explicit unit test)
- [x] New test passes a raw backslash-style pattern as CLI argv, not routed through the fixture-normalizing `fx()` helper
- [x] Non-Windows platforms pass `\`-containing patterns through unmodified
